title: One object under an S3 Lifecycle rule
claim: A lifecycle rule moves an object from one storage class to the next as the object gets older, and then the object expires.
alt: A timeline of object age with four marks: the day the object is created, then a later day, a much later day and a last day. The lifecycle rule sets the day numbers. From creation to the first mark the object is in S3 Standard and usual access is frequent. At the first mark a transition moves the object to S3 Standard-IA, and usual access is infrequent. At the second mark a second transition moves the object to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, and usual access is rare. On the last day the object expires.
notes: Pilot diagram. The day marks are words (Later, Much later, Last day) because the fact canon is still empty; replace them with day numbers from the canon before a chapter uses the figure. The minimum age for each transition is a hard fact and must come from the canon. The axis is not to scale. The access lane shows the access pattern that the rule assumes, not a property of the storage class. Check in the canon what expiration does in a bucket with versioning before a caption says that the object is deleted.
